question: In 2009, the European Union set itself the target of reaching 20 % renewables in its energy mix, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions by the same percentage by 2020. The EU met this target thanks to a regulatory framework that was clear and stable over time, and which notably encouraged Member States to move towards decarbonisation and electrification.

However, since 2024, we have witnessed the undermining of the existing regulatory framework, which is weakening its capacity to achieve the climate goals for 2030 and 2050 and creating uncertainty for some strategic sectors.

For example, the relaxing of measures prohibiting the sale of new internal combustion engine vehicles has led a number of organisations, such as the French electricity transmission network, to revise their electricity demand forecasts downwards.

This revision significantly affects the renewable energy sector, in particular the photovoltaic industry, which is seriously threatened by the negative outlook resulting from recent legislative developments. In view of this, what action does the Commission intend to take to protect sectors affected by the revision of the European regulatory framework, which is slowing down electrification in Europe?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2026) On 22 April 2026, the Commission adopted AccelerateEU1, a toolbox to bring immediate relief to households and industries following the effects of the conflict in the Middle East, while putting Europe on a pathway to energy independence.

The communication includes structural measures to further reduce dependency on volatile fossil fuel markets and build Europe's resilience against future risks based on homegrown clean energy and electrification. In 2024, 71% of the EU’s electricity generation came from clean energy sources, bringing cheap energy to the system. Nevertheless, electricity represents less than a quarter of the final energy consumption2.

This provides a clear case to accelerate electrification. In this framework, the Commission has committed to present an Electrification Action Plan, including an ambitious electrification target and addressing horizontal barriers to electrification, as well as sector-specific issues in the industrial, transport and building sectors.

Electrification is ramping up quickly in road transport, with more than 8 million battery electric vehicles on EU roads. The Automotive Package3 adopted by the Commission in December 2025 supports the sector’s transition to clean mobility by setting an ambitious yet pragmatic policy framework to ensure 2050 climate neutrality and strategic independence while providing more flexibility to manufacturers.

As part of the Package, the proposal amending the CO2 standards for cars and vans Regulation4 enhances technological neutrality while maintaining a clear market signal for electrification which will support continued investment by the EU industry in the transition and safeguard its ability to remain competitive.
1 AccelerateEU - Energy Union Affordable and Secure Energy through Accelerated Action Brussels, 22.4.2026
COM(2026) 370 final. 2 Eurostat data. 3 https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-themes/action-plan-future-automotive-sector/automotive-package_en. 4 COM/2025/995 final.
